The angle # potentials that need the distances between the atoms are therefore # turned into a CustomCompoundBondForce here, with the same energy # expression, parameters and angles. # OpenMM finds the parameters of an angle in either direction, but it # keeps the order of the atoms. The angles below are not the same in # both directions: their atoms have to be in this order of the classes, # which are given for each potential. atom_class = { "c1_1": "c1_b", "c3_1": "c3_b", "n1_1": "n1_b", } ordered = { "LINEAR_ANGLES": [ ( "c3_b", "c1_b", "n1_b" ), ], } classes = [atom_class.get(data.atomType[atom], "") for atom in data.atoms] for index in reversed(range(sys.getNumForces())): old = sys.getForce(index) if not isinstance(old, openmm.CustomAngleForce): continue energy = old.getEnergyFunction() if not "distance(" in energy: continue new = openmm.CustomCompoundBondForce(3, energy) new.setName(old.getName()) for i in range(old.getNumGlobalParameters()): name = old.getGlobalParameterName(i) new.addGlobalParameter(name, old.getGlobalParameterDefaultValue(i)) # The force gets the name of its potential if name.startswith("pot-"): new.setName(name[4:]) for i in range(old.getNumPerAngleParameters()): new.addPerBondParameter(old.getPerAngleParameterName(i)) order = ordered.get(new.getName(), []) for i in range(old.getNumAngles()): p1, p2, p3, params = old.getAngleParameters(i) if ( classes[p3], classes[p2], classes[p1] ) in order: p1, p3 = p3, p1 new.addBond([ p1, p2, p3 ], params) new.setForceGroup(old.getForceGroup()) new.setUsesPeriodicBoundaryConditions(old.usesPeriodicBoundaryConditions()) sys.removeForce(index) if new.getNumBonds() > 0: sys.addForce(new) </Script> <CustomNonbondedForce energy="4*epsilon*((sigma/r)^12 -
